body:
Concentrated triage batch: `finding` → `pm:queue`, Task (`domain:devx` stands) — re-triaged on the measurements: #11412's decision fence rested on an ASSUMED tension ("may be in tension" with `check:test-source-alias`), and this card measured the tension absent (anchor restored, gate green over 72 packages, zero test cost). #11412 itself is closed completed, so the fence's context is finished. Scope: land `server.deps.external` in `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` per the measured shape, pin the restored throw behaviour, keep `check:test-source-alias` green in the same PR. If a real conflict materializes that the measurement missed, stop and report — that would resurrect the decision, not bypass it.

**Claim** — `domain:devx @ objectstack` seat (#6023), session `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`.

- Branch: `claude/issue-11775-cli-vitest-deps-external`
- Worktree: `../objectstack-11775` (dedicated)
- Model tier: opus
- Clause ②: falsify, don't build on, this seat's assumptions.

**Declared file surface**: `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`, plus one `packages/cli` test file to pin the restored throw.

⚠️ **Cross-lane visibility note** (not a re-grading): the fix lands in `packages/cli`, which the domain table otherwise assigns to `domain:cli`. Triage re-triaged this card on 2026-08-25 and stated *"`domain:devx` stands"* deliberately, after the measurements — so this seat takes the label as given and claims it. Recorded here so a `domain:cli` seat scanning for file collisions can see this claim rather than discover it at merge time. ⛔ This seat does not produce `domain:*` and is not disputing it.

**Scope is triage's, quoted rather than paraphrased**: *"land `server.deps.external` in `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` per the measured shape, pin the restored throw behaviour, keep `check:test-source-alias` green in the same PR. If a real conflict materializes that the measurement missed, stop and report — that would resurrect the decision, not bypass it."*

{
  "issue": 11775,
  "status": "done",
  "branch": "claude/issue-11775-cli-vitest-deps-external",
  "pr": "https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12357",
  "premise_still_valid": true,
  "summary": "Landed `test.server.deps.external = [/packages[\/]types[\/]dist/]` in packages/cli/vitest.config.ts per the measured shape, and pinned the restored throw in test/vitest-resolution-base-collapse.e2e.test.ts. The card's premise holds: the anchor is restored (the in-process call now fails with real Node's own sentence, naming packages/types/dist/node.mjs as the base), check:test-source-alias stays green with readings IDENTICAL before and after (72 packages / 61 registered / 45 subpaths — the ledger moved in neither direction), and no test cost. ONE THING THE CARD'S MEASUREMENT MISSED, reported per the stop-and-report clause but assessed as NOT a resurrecting conflict: the card measured 11 files / 103 tests, but a 12th consumer landed 40 minutes AFTER the card was filed (#11771, 2026-08-24T16:40:59Z vs card 16:00:13Z) — vitest-resolution-base-collapse.e2e.test.ts, which pins the COLLAPSE. 103 + its 9 cases = the 112 I measured. Landing the entry turns exactly 2 of its 9 cases red. Those 2 assert the ABSENCE of the anchor this card exists to restore, so their inversion IS the fix landing, not a collision: the gate stays green, nothing moved off source, the other 11 files are 103/103 identical, and that file's own header instructs re-measurement in precisely this event ('If this ever reads false, M1 is gone and the two cases above should be re-measured'). I re-measured and rewrote them rather than deleting them; PM should confirm this reading of scope, since it is the one judgement call in the card.",
  "tests": "ALL exit codes captured before any pipe (redirect-then-tail, or PIPESTATUS). Heavy work serialized through scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh; verdicts read from its VERDICT line, never a bare $?.

POSITIVE CONTROL ON THE PATTERN (Zone 2b — the trap that fails silently), against the real resolved realpath /home/user/objectstack-11775/packages/types/dist/node.js: measured shape /packages[\/]types[\/]dist/ => MATCH; natural-looking /@objectstack[\/]types/ => NO MATCH; vitest default /\/node_modules\// => NO MATCH (which is exactly why it was inlined). No negative result in this card was accepted without this control.

BEFORE (baseline, 12 consumer files): 'Test Files 12 passed (12) / Tests 112 passed (112)'.
AFTER (same 12): 2 failed / 110 passed — both in the collapse pin, with 'AssertionError: promise rejected "Error: Cannot find package 'chalk'..." instead of resolving' and the caused-by naming 'imported from /home/user/objectstack-11775/packages/types/dist/node.mjs' — i.e. the anchor restored, in-process reading == real-Node reading.
AFTER REWRITING THE PIN (same 12): 'Test Files 12 passed (12) / Tests 112 passed (112)'. Re-run at final post-merge HEAD 77a2741: same, 12/12 and 112/112.

FULL packages/cli SUITE (the card ran 11 of its files; I ran all 183 / 2090 tests, in 4 chunks to stay under the container's ~10min foreground cap): 39f/444t, 44f/532t, 52f/677t, 48f/437t — all passing. Two reds surfaced and NEITHER was this change: (a) serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts 'Error: command serve not found' — packages/cli/dist did not exist (I had built only its dependency closure) and that file deliberately spawns the SHIPPED bin/run.js; after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli build` it is 3/3 green. (b) serve-mcp-stdio-answers.e2e.test.ts 'TypeError: fetch failed / ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:43054' — a spawned-server boot race under container load (that chunk took 462s); 1/1 green in isolation, and structurally unreachable by this change since the spawned child is a separate process with its own resolution.

ABLATION (Zone 2c — proving the pin can fail). Mutation confirmed ON DISK, not by an editor's exit code: deleted-text grep count 0 and '^  test: {' count 0, plus a changed git hash-object. Result: 'Tests 2 failed | 7 passed (9)' — exactly the 2 new cases, ABLATION_EXIT=1. Restore under trap ... EXIT INT TERM, proved byte-identical: restored hash b7b04d2d5166af496c8de96447c7af25378eda61 == expected, marker back.
REBUILD LEG — does it apply? Stated explicitly: NO, and here is why. Both ablation legs read the SAME packages/types/dist/node.mjs; the mutation is in the vitest config only, so it changes whether Vite inlines that file, never the file's bytes. Staleness could still fake a green in a different way (dist behind src, both legs measuring old behaviour), so that was closed separately: 0 files under packages/types/src are newer than dist/node.mjs (dist built 18:15:46, newest src 18:09:36).

ZONE 2D — the card's load-bearing structural claim, MEASURED rather than argued. Claim: a /dist/-anchored external cannot match a package aliased to source. It holds, and for a stronger reason than the card gives: resolve.alias acts in the RESOLVE phase, so an aliased specifier is already an absolute src/... path before the externalise predicate is consulted — and check:test-source-alias is the gate that FAILS any alias whose winning entry does not land under src/. The gate assumed to be in tension with this entry is the same gate that enforces the disjointness. Direct experiment: with the source alias for @objectstack/service-cache AND a /service-cache[\/]dist/ external both present, a marker planted only in src (grep: 1 in src, 0 in dist/index.js) was the one that loaded — result SRC. Both mutations restored under trap, both proved byte-identical by git hash-object (cfg and src).

ZONE 2E — unmeasured second-order costs, checked against packages/cli as it stands: NO vi.mock/vi.doMock of @objectstack/types anywhere in the package; its only mock targets are ../utils/optional-package.js (3), node:fs/promises (1), @objectstack/cloud-connection (1). So the vi.mock cost does not bite. Coverage instrumentation of the externalised package IS genuinely lost; recorded in the config header for whoever extends the list.

GATE UNION derived at the FINAL commit with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`. First derivation printed ⚠️ STALE TREE (10 commits behind, 8 gate-source files changed) — merged origin/main and re-derived; second run clean at 77a27419f5, --repo assertion holds, 2-path change set, 16 matched families.
GREEN (exit captured pre-pipe): check:test-source-alias, cli-test-child-env, cross-package-test-inputs, type-source-resolution, published-files, page-declaration-shape, slot-lookup, nul-bytes, engine-double-contract, where-matcher, query-options-erasure, type-check-coverage, i18n, i18n-coverage, check-ci-filter-parity.mjs, check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs, check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs, docs-audit/check-affected-docs.mjs, docs-audit/check-drift-comment.mjs, plus `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` (TYPECHECK_EXIT=0, script name echoed so it is not a zero-match false green).
Two gates initially returned PREREQUISITE-style refusals, which are NOT MEASURED, never failures: check:i18n-coverage said 'COULD NOT MEASURE — 1 of 12 config(s) failed to lint' on unbuilt connector-mcp/connector-openapi; after building the showcase closure it is genuinely GREEN ('OK (12 config(s), 657 baselined untranslated string(s), none new)').
⚠️ check:type-check-debt is NOT MEASURED and is NOT reported green: its --re-measure leg first refused outright ('cannot run: 1 workspace dependenc(ies) ... no built type entry point'), and after building that dependency the retry hit the container's ~10min foreground cap (exit 143). Its structural half, check:type-check-coverage, DID run and printed OK. CI owns the ratchet. Lock checked afterwards — released cleanly, no orphaned holder.

No changeset, reasoned rather than assumed: packages/cli publishes only [dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md]; neither edited file reaches dist/ (verified against the freshly built dist), so nothing user-visible ships. skip-changeset applied and READ BACK: labels are now [size/m, tests, skip-changeset]. Note the additive POST /labels endpoint was blocked for this seat by the permission classifier, so I DECLARE the documented fallback: read -> union -> whole-set write. The read-back also shows the union preserved the `tests` label that automation added between my read and my write.",
  "open_questions": [],
  "out_of_scope_findings": []
}
